title: Bossam
subtitle: korean boiled pork with wraps
excerpt: Bossam is Korean boiled pork belly simmered until very tender in a spiced broth, then served in slices with napa cabbage leaves, fermented kimchi, garlic, and dipping sauce for wrapping and eating by hand. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Bossam is a classic Korean pork dish. It is traditionally eaten during kimchi-making season in late autumn and winter, when freshly made kimchi is served alongside.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked pork in slices for up to 2 months. Reheat gently in a covered pan with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Cook a larger joint and slice as needed. Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the pork a day ahead and refrigerate. Slice and reheat gently before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: A type of whole-leaf kimchi made especially to accompany bossam pork. Fresh leaves are used as wrappers rather than fermented ones.
A thick Korean dipping sauce made from doenjang (soybean paste), gochujang, garlic, and sesame oil. It is essential for Korean pork wraps.

content.text: Bossam is served with wrapping leaves,
sauce, and a selection of condiments. Each diner builds their own wraps at the table. Serves 4.
The poaching liquid is flavoured with garlic, ginger, and doenjang paste, which removes the pork's strong smell and adds depth.
or regular kimchi on the side completes the dish.
Place the pork belly in a large saucepan. Cover with cold water, bring to a boil, and blanch for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.

Return the pork to the pan. Add the poaching liquid ingredients and enough fresh water to cover. Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cover and cook for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until the pork is very tender when pierced with a knife.
Lift the pork from the liquid and rest for 10 minutes. Slice into 5 mm pieces across the grain, keeping both the fat and lean layers intact.
Mix the ssamjang ingredients together. Arrange the cabbage leaves, sliced garlic, and spring onion on a serving plate.
Place a slice of pork on a cabbage leaf. Add a sliver of garlic, a little spring onion, and a dab of ssamjang. Fold the leaf around the filling and eat in one or two bites.

attrs.issue: Pork is still firm after 1 hour
attrs.fix: Continue simmering with the lid on. The pork is done when a knife slides in easily. Some pieces may take up to 90 minutes.
The blanching step reduces this. Make sure to drain and rinse the pork fully after the first boil before adding the clean poaching liquid.

attrs.issue: Slices are falling apart when cutting
attrs.fix: Let the pork rest longer before slicing. Cold pork slices more cleanly. You can refrigerate it fully and slice cold, then reheat the slices gently.

content.text: Bossam is closely linked to kimchi-making season in Korea. Families traditionally made it to feed the people who came together to make a year's supply of kimchi. It is now a popular restaurant dish and a common choice for shared family meals. The pork is eaten wrapped, with generous dipping and lots of kimchi on the side.
